rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Chap. LVIII. If the Querent have open Enemies, or any Adversaries or many that doe envy him.
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The chapter heading asks whether the querent has enemies or adversaries, including people alleged to envy them.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Original PDF417/printed383 below the LVII/LVIII divider; previous section on potential fighting belongs to LVII.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: difficult Question, and yet by Astrologie responsible
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author presents the question as difficult but in his view answerable through astrology.
rows.conditions_and_limits: An author assertion, not empirical verification.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Have I enemies or not?
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He explicitly distinguishes the general existence-of-enemies question.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Source paragraph begins on PDF417 and continues on PDF418.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Whether is such a man my adversary?
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He also distinguishes the question about a particular nominated person.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Do not use the broad twelfth-house test as a shortcut for the named-person case.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: But if the querent doubt his Brother, Father, or Servant
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Original marginal note distinguishes suspected relatives or a servant from an arbitrary nominated party.
rows.conditions_and_limits: This is part of the historical classification only, not proof of anyone's hostility.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: take Signification from each particular House
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author says to consider each named relationship's own house.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Do not default every relative to the ordinary seventh-house stranger assignment.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: If any be nominated, require judgment from the seventh house and Lord
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: A specifically nominated person is first evaluated by the seventh and its lord.
rows.conditions_and_limits: The margin qualifies family/servant cases separately.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the seventh aspect the Lord of the ascendant ... square or opposition
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: A hard square/opposition from seventh lord to ascendant lord is one original source test.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Explicit aspect to first lord; not any seventh-house placement.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: or be in like aspect with the Moon
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: A corresponding square/opposition to Moon is an alternative.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Preserve the OR alternative.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: party enquired after doth envy the Querent, and wishes him no good
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Under the hard-aspect branches the author attributes ill will to a nominated person.
rows.conditions_and_limits: This is NOT a demonstrated fact about that person or any present-day relationship.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: if the aspect be separated
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The original differentiates a separating aspect from an applying one.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Applies to the preceding hard-aspect test.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: they have lately been in some contest
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: With separation the author speculates about recent disagreement.
rows.conditions_and_limits: No case outcome independently authenticated.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: if ... applying to a square or opposition
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: An applying hard aspect is a separate condition.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Do not treat as the same tense as separating.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: enmity ... approaching ... grow to a greater height
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He conjectures that conflict continues or worsens under application.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Untested future-event assertion and mind-reading allegation.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the seventh be in the twelfth from the ascendant
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author names the seventh lord in the twelfth house as another source condition.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Do not conflate with relative sign positions.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: in the twelft signe from the place wherein the Lord of the ascendant is
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He also considers the twelfth sign reckoned from the ascendant lord's position.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Original turned-sign counting convention not formalized here.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: or from the place wherein the Moon is
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The twelfth-sign placement relative to Moon is a further alternative.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Not the same as the direct twelfth house.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the seventh be in conjunction with any Planet
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: A conjunction involving the seventh lord and another planet begins a longer alternative.
rows.conditions_and_limits: The relevance depends on what other planet connects to the first lord or Moon.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: or in any aspect with a Planet ... conjunction or square to the Lord of the ascendant or the Moon
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The text also describes an intermediary planet connecting to the first lord or Moon by conjunction or square.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Grammar of conjunction/aspect alternation retained without inventing a scored graph.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: without Reception
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The text explicitly excludes reception for the intermediary hard-aspect branch.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Scope over every preceding OR is uncertain; do not remove this condition.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: then the Quesited ... is averse, and an enemy
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Under the preceding named-person configurations the author labels the nominee hostile.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Unverified allegation; never use as real accusation of an identifiable person.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: but if it be not so ... no enemy
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The text supplies a negative conclusion if the specified configurations are absent.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Do not treat silence, other charts, or unknown responses as positive evidence.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: If the Question be absolute ... Whether have I enemies, yea or no?
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author returns to the general, unnamed-enemies question.
rows.conditions_and_limits: This distinct branch excludes nominated-person readings.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: require judgment herein from the twelfth house
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The twelfth and its lord signify hidden opposition in the author's general-question framework.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Source-native house meaning only.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of [twelfth] be in square or opposition to the Moon
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The twelfth lord aspecting Moon by square/opposition is offered as a general-question condition.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Requires the specific two signs/lords, not all twelfth-house aspects.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: with or without Reception
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Unlike the nominated intermediary branch, the source allows the aspect with OR without reception.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Preserve the distinct reception rule.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: he hath enemies that watch for an opportunity against him
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author conjectures concealed adversaries.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Never applied to a current person's real safety or suspicions.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: they doe all things clandestinely and cunningly
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Lilly elaborates that the supposed enemies may act covertly.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Not evidence of a conspiracy.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: still goe under the notion of Friends
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He conjectures disguised friendship as another interpretation.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Unverified claim and especially vulnerable to unfalsifiable retrospective fitting.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Consider also where and in what house the Lord of the twelfth is
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author proposes considering the house placement of the twelfth lord to describe alleged adversaries.
rows.conditions_and_limits: No fixed verified psychological profiler.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Many Planets in the seventh, denotes many enemies
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He equates many seventh-house planets with many adversaries.
rows.conditions_and_limits: No count threshold or independent population-base-rate data supplied.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Often and ever by me found true.
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The original margin contains a first-person assertion of repeated success.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Anecdotal author claim; NOT an audited empirical test or reproducible case count.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: many Planets in the second
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author includes a separate multiple-planet-second-house observation.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Do not confuse this with seventh-house enemy-count rule.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: much want of money, if they are ill dignified
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: He associates an ill-dignified second-house cluster with financial lack.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Explicit ill-dignity condition; no actual financial case evidence.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: what houses they are Lords of ... quality of people
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Planets in the seventh and the houses those planets rule are used to conjecture descriptions of supposed adversaries.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Source passage continues from PDF418 to PDF419; no person-specific profiling is validated.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: square aspect shewes envy and malice, yet possible to be reconciled
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: The author treats square as alleging ill will yet permitting reconciliation.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Only a literal source claim; not advice about identifying hostile relationships.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: opposition aspects without Reception, never
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Without reception, opposition is described as an enduring obstacle to reconciliation.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Reception absence is explicit. A categorical 'never' is the author's rhetoric, not observed certainty.

rows.source_short_anchor_not_diplomatic: Chap. LIX. A Lady, if marry the Gentleman desired?
rows.historical_claim_paraphrase: Chapter LIX begins below the original divider on PDF419/printed385 and contains a worked chart.
rows.conditions_and_limits: Navigation marker only; the chart and its analysis are for the next source batch.
